analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and a principal cause of cervical cancer, yet comprehensive and updated data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in Isfahan, central Iran, remain limited despite regional reports.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results from 4,973 women screened between 2015 and 2024 at a referral laboratory in Isfahan, central Iran.
analysis_en.methods: The study collected and analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results alongside available demographic data from women referred for genital HPV screening.
analysis_en.main_results: Of 4,973 women screened, 819 (16.5%) tested HPV-positive, with HPV6 being the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types were slightly more frequent than low-risk types (55.2% vs. 44.8%), with HPV16 (14.4%) the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV53 (13.2%) and HPV18 (6.2%). HPV positivity was highest in women under 20 years of age (27.3%; P = 0.002).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high HPV infection rate in Isfahan as comparable to other regions in Iran and noted that more than half of HPV-positive women were infected with high-risk types, highlighting the burden of oncogenic HPV in the population.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a substantial burden of HPV infection and high-risk genotypes in Isfahan, which may inform local vaccination strategies and cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on a single referral laboratory limit generalizability, and the absence of clinical outcomes or longitudinal follow-up reduces the strength of evidence for causal inference.

papers.title_zh: 2015年至2024年伊朗中部伊斯法罕女性人乳头瘤病毒类型患病率的回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes the most prevalent sexually transmitted infection and is the principal cause of cervical cancer. Despite several regional reports from Iran, comprehensive and updated data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among women in Isfahan, central Iran, remain limited. The present study aimed to determine the prevalence of HPV infection and HPV types in the recordings of women referred for genital HPV screening to a Medical Laboratory in Isfahan, central Iran. In this retrospective study, HPV PCR and genotyping results of 4,973 women and their available demographic data screened between 2015 and 2024 at a referral laboratory in Isfahan were collected, analyzed and reported. Of 4,973 women screened, 819 (16.5%) tested HPV-positive. HPV6 was the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types were slightly more frequent than low-risk types (55.2% vs. 44.8%), with HPV16 (14.4%) the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV53 (13.2%) and HPV18 (6.2%). HPV positivity was highest in women under 20 years of age (27.3%; P = 0.002). Based on the results of the present study, the rate of HPV infection in Isfahan was high, yet comparable to that reported in several other regions in Iran. More than half of HPV-positive women were infected with high-risk types in Isfahan area. Among the tested population, the highest positivity was observed in women under 20 years old.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 引起最流行的性传播感染,也是 宫颈癌 的主要原因。尽管伊朗发布了几份区域报告,但有关伊朗中部伊斯法罕妇女中 HPV 患病率 和基因型分布的全面和最新数据仍然有限。本研究旨在确定转介至伊朗中部伊斯法罕医学实验室进行生殖器 HPV 筛查的女性记录中 HPV 感染的 患病率 和 HPV 类型。在这项回顾性研究中,收集、分析和报告了 2015 年至 2024 年间在伊斯法罕转诊实验室筛查的 4,973 名女性的 HPV PCR 和基因分型结果及其可用的人口统计数据。在接受筛查的 4,973 名女性中,819 名 (16.5%) 检测出 HPV 呈阳性。HPV6 是最常见的基因型(9.2%)。在HPV阳性女性中,高危型的发生率略高于低危型(55.2% vs. 44.8%),其中HPV16(14.4%)是最常见的高危基因型,其次是HPV53(13.2%)和HPV18(6.2%)。20 岁以下女性的 HPV 阳性率最高(27.3%;P = 0.002)。根据本研究的结果,伊斯法罕的 HPV 感染率很高,但与伊朗其他几个地区报告的情况相当。在伊斯法罕地区,超过一半的HPV阳性女性感染了高危型。在受测人群中,20岁以下的女性阳性率最高。

papers.title: Correlation between high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) viral load and cervical lesions across different subtypes, along with the development of a clinical prediction model
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective The study aims to investigate the correlation between the viral loads of HPV16/18 and 16 other high-risk HPV types (designated as non-16/18 group) and the severity of cervical lesions, and to develop a HSIL+ risk prediction model to furnish evidence for pragmatic clinical triage and precision management strategies. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the data from 331 HR-HPV-positive patients collected between July 2025 and January 2026. Using a semi-quantitative hybrid capture-chemiluminescence platform,The viral loads of HPV16/18 and non-16/18 group were measured, and patients were categorized into normal, LSIL, HSIL, and cervical cancer groups based on pathological findings. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was employed to examine the associations among viral load, HPV subtypes, age, and lesion severity, and a HSIL+ prediction nomogram was constructed. Results The prevalence of HPV16/18 infection escalated with increasing lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cervical cancer: OR=23.28), demonstrating a pattern of “continuous augmentation”. Conversely, the viral load of non-16/18 group increased during the LSIL and HSIL stages but declined in the cancer stage, exhibiting a pattern of “early involvement followed by later attenuation”. While single non-16/18 group infections demonstrated early warning value, HPV16/18 types and medium to high viral loads were identified as independent risk factors for HSIL+. The nomogram underwent Bootstrap validation and yielded an AUC of 0.763, indicating satisfactory calibration. Conclusion This study comprehensively analyzed the pathogenic features of viral loads associated with HPV16/18 and other high-risk subtypes, elucidating the lesion patterns of distinct subtypes. While HPV16/18 acts as the principal persistent driver, the high viral load of the non-16/18 group provides a critical "window-of-opportunity" indication during the precancerous phase. A pragmatic HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram was devised to serve as an accessible clinical aid for the early identification of high-risk lesions, thereby optimizing real-world personalized management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly HPV16/18, is a principal driver of cervical carcinogenesis, yet the relationship between viral load and lesion severity across HPV subtypes remains incompletely defined. The study sought to quantify this association and to derive a clinical tool to guide triage of HPV-positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients whose data were collected between July 2025 and January 2026. Patients were stratified by HPV subtype (HPV16/18 versus 16 other high-risk types) and by cervical lesion severity into normal, LSIL, HSIL, and cervical cancer groups.
analysis.methods: Viral loads for HPV16/18 and the non-16/18 group were measured using a semi-quantitative hybrid capture–chemiluminescence platform. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess associations among viral load, HPV subtype, age, and lesion severity, and a HSIL+ risk prediction nomogram was constructed and validated by bootstrap.
analysis.main_results: HPV16/18 infection prevalence increased with lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cervical cancer: OR=23.28), while non-16/18 viral load rose during LSIL and HSIL but declined in cancer. HPV16/18 types and medium-to-high viral loads were identified as independent risk factors for HSIL+, and the nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.763.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret HPV16/18 as the principal persistent driver of progression, whereas high non-16/18 viral load signals a critical precancerous window. They report a novel HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram that integrates subtype-specific viral load and age for pragmatic clinical triage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support subtype-aware, viral-load–based triage to prioritize high-risk HPV-positive patients for early colposcopy or intervention, potentially reducing overtreatment and improving resource allocation in cervical cancer prevention programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design, single-center sampling, and reliance on semi-quantitative viral load measurement limit causal inference and generalizability; bootstrap validation yielded moderate discrimination (AUC 0.763), indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients collected between July 2025 and January 2026 examined how viral loads of HPV16/18 and 16 other high-risk types correlate with cervical lesion severity. HPV16/18 and medium-to-high viral loads were independent HSIL+ risk factors, and a bootstrap-validated nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.763. The authors conclude that HPV16/18 acts as the principal persistent driver, while high non-16/18 viral load provides an early warning during precancer. elements_zh.methods: 使用半定量混合捕获-化学发光平台测量 HPV16/18 和非 16/18 组的病毒载量。使用多变量逻辑回归评估病毒载量、HPV 亚型、年龄和病变严重程度之间的关联,并构建 HSIL+ 风险预测列线图并通过 bootstrap 进行验证。

papers.title: Immunological and antitumor responses to HPV-targeted therapeutic vaccines in preclinical models of head and neck cancer: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is increasingly prevalent and accounts for 22-70% of HNSCCs depending on the region. Although prophylactic HPV vaccines were approved in the early 2000s to prevent HPV infection and oncogenesis, they are ineffective against established HPV infections and related cancers. The standard of care for these HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers combines radiotherapy, surgery, and chemotherapy. However, these treatments can result in significant lifelong side effects for patients with no new treatments entering regular clinical practice in the past decade. Therapeutic cancer vaccines represent an opportunity for novel treatment approaches in HPV-associated cancer, particularly because these cancers display viral tumor-specific antigens (TSAs) such as E6 and E7, making them easily targetable by this type of immunotherapy. Currently, there are no FDA-approved therapeutic vaccines for HPV-associated cancers, but preclinical and clinical studies are ongoing in this area. In this systematic review, we describe current HPV vaccination strategies, their biological mechanisms, and their immunological and therapeutic effects in preclinical cancer models. We discuss each component of therapeutic vaccines: antigens, delivery platforms, adjuvants, and combination agents. We also assess the results of recent preclinical studies evaluating HPV therapeutic vaccines to provide an outlook on the future of this treatment modality.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述将 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 作为目标病原体和疾病,重点关注临床前模型中的治疗 疫苗。核心问题涉及 HPV 相关 HNSCC 临床前研究中 HPV 靶向治疗药物 疫苗 引起的免疫和抗肿瘤反应。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇系统综述,综合了 HPV 治疗药物 疫苗 的临床前研究,详细介绍了 疫苗 的组成部分(抗原、递送平台、佐剂和组合药物),并评估了临床前癌症模型中的免疫学和治疗效果。该综述明确将其范围界定为描述当前的 HPV 疫苗接种 策略及其在临床前背景下的生物学机制。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该审查强调,HPV 相关的 HNSCC 是一种重大的疾病负担,根据地区的不同,HPV 占 HNSCC 的 22-70%。它强调治疗性 疫苗 利用病毒肿瘤特异性抗原,例如 E6 和 E7,这些抗原很容易被 HPV 相关癌症的免疫疗法靶向。此外,该审查指出,尽管正在进行临床前和临床研究,但 FDA 尚未批准用于 HPV 相关癌症的治疗药物 疫苗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查发现了一个关键差距:虽然预防性 HPV 疫苗 可有效对抗感染和肿瘤发生,但它们对已确定的 HPV 感染和相关癌症无效,从而留下治疗空白。它还指出,针对 HPV 相关口咽癌(放疗、手术和化疗)的标准 治疗 可能会导致显着的终生副作用,这强调了对新治疗方法的需求。

papers.title: Improving cervical cancer screening uptake through theory-informed education: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: This study examined whether theory-based education increases cervical cancer screening among underserved women. METHODS: Seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) were systematically searched for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025. A total of 1,200 records were identified; after duplicate removal, 900 titles and abstracts were screened, and 200 full-text articles were assessed. Fourteen studies met inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis, and 12 trials contributed extractable binary outcome data for meta-analysis, including one study with two distinct intervention arms. The primary outcome was screening uptake (Pap smear, visual inspection with acetic acid [VIA], or human papillomavirus [HPV] testing). Data extraction and quality appraisal followed PRISMA 2020 and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, and heterogeneity, prediction intervals, small-study effects, and certainty of evidence (GRADE) were evaluated. RESULTS: Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care or minimal information (OR = 4.41; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.21-8.80). Subgroup analyses showed substantial effects in both high-income (OR = 3.46; 95% CI: 1.43-8.36) and middle-income settings (OR = 6.55; 95% CI: 2.74-15.63). Interventions frequently incorporated behavioral frameworks, such as the Health Belief Model, Protection Motivation Theory, and BASNEF model, and were often culturally tailored or delivered through community-embedded formats. INTERPRETATION: Integrating such interventions into national and local screening programs represents an effective and equitable strategy to reduce disparities in cervical cancer prevention.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether theory-informed educational interventions increase uptake of cervical cancer screening among underserved women, focusing on human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical cancer prevention and screening modalities such as Pap smear, VIA, or HPV testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that searched seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025, identifying 1,200 records, screening 900 titles and abstracts, and assessing 200 full-text articles; 14 studies were included in qualitative synthesis and 12 trials contributed data for meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care or minimal information (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with substantial effects observed in both high-income (OR = 3.46; 95% CI: 1.43–8.36) and middle-income settings (OR = 6.55; 95% CI: 2.74–15.63).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review did not report on the long-term sustainability of intervention effects, differential impacts across specific underserved subgroups, or the cost-effectiveness of theory-informed education programs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating theory-based educational interventions into national and local cervical cancer screening programs is recommended to reduce disparities in HPV-associated cervical cancer prevention, particularly in underserved populations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether theory-informed educational interventions improve cervical cancer screening uptake among underserved women. Using a comprehensive search across seven databases from 2005 to 2025, 14 studies were synthesized qualitatively and 12 trials were included in a meta-analysis. Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with notable effects in both high-income and middle-income settings. Interventions frequently incorporated behavioral frameworks such as the Health Belief Model and were often culturally tailored or community-embedded. The review concludes that integrating these interventions into screening programs could effectively reduce disparities in HPV-associated cervical cancer prevention.

papers.title: Strengthening Adolescent Sexual Health Literacy through Targeted Educational Interventions in German Secondary Schools.
papers.abstract: Adolescents are a key population in STI prevention, yet many lack foundational knowledge and access to reliable information. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a targeted sexual health education lecture on knowledge about STIs and HPV vaccination as well as behavioral intentions in Bavaria, Germany. We conducted a prospective, anonymized survey with students from secondary schools across Bavaria. An online questionnaire was completed before (t = 1; n = 5,988) and after (t = 2; n = 4,739) a standardized, extracurricular sexual health lecture. Participants were aged 14-20 years (mean age 16.1), from diverse school types. Key outcomes included self-assessed knowledge, ability to explain specific STIs, awareness of the HPV vaccine, and willingness to receive the vaccination. Self-reported STI knowledge increased significantly: only 29.1% of students felt well-informed at baseline, compared to 85.96% after the lecture. The average number of STIs students could explain rose from 1.91 to 6.49 (p < 0.001). HIV/AIDS was the most well-understood STI pre-intervention (69.9%), rising to 89.3% post-intervention. Uncertainty about STI transmission decreased from 20.3% to 5.0%. HPV vaccine awareness increased from 75.1% to 95.3%. Among those not vaccinated, willingness to receive the vaccine significantly improved (mean score 2.95 to 3.53 on a 5-point scale, p < 0.001). A single, structured sexual health lecture significantly improved adolescent knowledge of STIs, reduced misinformation, and increased willingness to engage in preventive behaviors, including HPV vaccination. These findings support integrating educational interventions into broader public health strategies targeting youth to reduce long-term infection risks and promote informed decision-making.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述考察了德国巴伐利亚州有针对性的性健康教育讲座对青少年有关性传播感染 (STI) 和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 的知识及其行为意图的影响。核心问题集中于结构化教育干预是否可以提高性传播感染知识、减少错误信息并提高参与预防行为的意愿,包括 14-20 岁青少年中的 HPV 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论描述了一项针对巴伐利亚中学生进行的前瞻性匿名调查。在标准化课外性健康讲座之前(n = 5,988)和之后(n = 4,739)进行了在线调查问卷。参与者年龄为 14-20 岁(平均年龄 16.1 岁),代表不同类型的学校。主要结果包括自我评估的性传播感染知识、解释特定性传播感染的能力、对 HPV 疫苗 的认识以及接受 疫苗接种 的意愿。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查报告称,教育干预后青少年的知识和意识显着提高。自我报告的性传播感染知识从 29.1% 增加到 85.96%,学生能够解释的性传播感染平均数量从 1.91 增加到 6.49 (p < 0.001)。对艾滋病毒/艾滋病的了解从 69.9% 提高到 89.3%,对性传播感染 传播 的不确定性从 20.3% 下降到 5.0%。HPV 疫苗 认知度从 75.1% 提高到 95.3%,未接种疫苗的学生接受 疫苗 的意愿显着提高(5 分制平均分 2.95 至 3.53,p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查不报告长期随访数据来评估知识保留或行为改变的持久性。此外,该研究依赖于自我报告的数据,这可能会引入反应偏差。该审查并未解决巴伐利亚州不同社会经济或文化亚群体之间干预效果的潜在差异。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议将结构化的性健康教育讲座纳入针对青少年的公共卫生战略,以降低感染风险并促进知情决策。未来的研究应评估此类干预措施的长期影响,并探索解决服务不足人群知识差距的策略。

papers.title: mRNA Vaccines Targeting HPV E6/E7: A New Frontier in Cervical Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, particularly high-risk types 16 and 18, are responsible for approximately 70% of cervical cancer cases worldwide. Despite the availability of effective prophylactic vaccines, therapeutic interventions for established HPV-associated malignancies remain limited. This mini-review synthesizes recent advances (2020-2026) in mRNA-LNP vaccine development targeting the HPV E6 and E7 oncoproteins. We examine the mechanistic basis for targeting E6/E7, technological advantages of mRNA-LNP platforms, and key preclinical evidence demonstrating potent T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity. Recent clinical progress, including BioNTech's BNT113 vaccine which received FDA Fast Track designation for HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, is discussed alongside ongoing challenges in delivery optimization, tumor microenvironment immunosuppression, and manufacturing scalability. The review concludes with future perspectives on combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and the potential for personalized neoantigen approaches.

papers.title: Liquid Biopsy in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review of the Scientific Literature.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) presents a significant global health challenge, characterized by late-stage diagnosis and high rates of locoregional recurrence. Traditional tissue biopsy, while considered the gold standard, is invasive and often fails to capture the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of the tumor. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative, noninvasive paradigm for molecular diagnostics, leveraging circulating biomarkers found in blood and saliva. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence regarding the diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity of circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and the transcriptomic landscape of coding and noncoding RNAs (miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs) in HNSCC. Our review highlights the specificity of ctDNA for monitoring minimal residual disease, particularly in human papillomavirus- and Epstein-Barr virus-driven malignancies, where viral kinetics serve as sensitive biomarkers for recurrence. Furthermore, we explore the utility of "Saliva-Exosomics," suggesting that salivary exosomes may offer high sensitivity for early-stage oral cavity lesions due to anatomical proximity. The review also synthesizes data on novel RNA species, such as tumor-educated platelets and circular RNAs, which act as stable systemic biosensors. Despite promising results, significant heterogeneity in isolation protocols and detection platforms (e.g., next-generation sequencing vs. digital PCR) remains a barrier to widespread clinical implementation. We conclude that integrating multianalyte liquid biopsies into clinical practice holds the potential to personalize therapeutic strategies, improve survival outcomes, and redefine the standard of care in head and neck oncology.

papers.source_body_en: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) presents a significant global health challenge, characterized by late-stage diagnosis and high rates of locoregional recurrence. Traditional tissue biopsy, while considered the gold standard, is invasive and often fails to capture the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of the tumor. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative, noninvasive paradigm for molecular diagnostics, leveraging circulating biomarkers found in blood and saliva. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence regarding the diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity of circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and the transcriptomic landscape of coding and noncoding RNAs (miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs) in HNSCC. Our review highlights the specificity of ctDNA for monitoring minimal residual disease, particularly in human papillomavirus- and Epstein-Barr virus-driven malignancies, where viral kinetics serve as sensitive biomarkers for recurrence. Furthermore, we explore the utility of "Saliva-Exosomics," suggesting that salivary exosomes may offer high sensitivity for early-stage oral cavity lesions due to anatomical proximity. The review also synthesizes data on novel RNA species, such as tumor-educated platelets and circular RNAs, which act as stable systemic biosensors. Despite promising results, significant heterogeneity in isolation protocols and detection platforms (e.g., next-generation sequencing vs. digital PCR) remains a barrier to widespread clinical implementation. We conclude that integrating multianalyte liquid biopsies into clinical practice holds the potential to personalize therapeutic strategies, improve survival outcomes, and redefine the standard of care in head and neck oncology.
papers.abstract_zh: 头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 是一项重大的全球健康挑战,其特点是晚期 诊断 和高局部区域复发率。传统的组织活检虽然被认为是金标准,但具有侵入性,通常无法捕获肿瘤的空间和时间异质性。液体活检已成为一种革命性的、无创的分子诊断范例,利用血液和唾液中发现的循环生物标志物。本系统综述严格评估了有关 HNSCC 中循环肿瘤细胞、循环肿瘤 DNA (ctDNA) 以及编码和非编码 RNA(miRNA、lncRNA 和 circRNA)转录组学景观的诊断准确性、预后价值和分子有效性的当前证据。我们的综述强调了 ctDNA 在监测微小残留病方面的特异性,特别是在 人乳头瘤病毒 和 Epstein-Barr 病毒驱动的恶性肿瘤中,其中病毒动力学可作为复发的敏感生物标志物。此外,我们探索了“唾液外泌体”的实用性,表明唾液外泌体由于解剖学上的接近性可能对早期口腔病变具有高敏感性。该综述还综合了新型 RNA 种类的数据,例如肿瘤培养的血小板和环状 RNA,它们可作为稳定的全身生物传感器。尽管结果有希望,但分离方案和检测平台(例如下一代测序与数字 PCR)的显着异质性仍然是广泛临床实施的障碍。我们的结论是,将多分析物液体活检纳入临床实践有可能实现个性化治疗策略、改善生存结果并重新定义头颈肿瘤学的护理标准。

papers.title: Addressing HPV vaccine hesitancy and misinformation in India through public health communication strategies.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT India witnessed a significant step forward in cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage with the rollout of a nationwide free HPV vaccination drive aimed at vaccinating 14‐y‐old girls. However, the campaign’s success rate can be significantly reduced if timely measures to tackle vaccine hesitancy and related misinformation are not taken into account. This commentary article discusses the effects of HPV vaccine misinformation, identifies global vaccine hesitancy factors, and highlights behavioral determinants affecting HPV vaccine hesitancy and its coverage in India. It identifies low awareness, misconceptions, sociocultural beliefs, stigma, safety concerns, weak injunctive norms, parental resistance, urban–rural disparities, and health system barriers as key challenges associated with vaccine hesitancy and low vaccine uptake among adolescents in India. Using an integrated Health Belief Model (HBM) and COM-B theoretical framework, it proposes a culturally sensitive, evidence-based multifactorial communication strategy focused on raising awareness, building trust, countering misinformation, capacity building of healthcare providers, and enhancing opportunities for the adoption of HPV preventive behavior. The commentary highlights the need to actively engage parents, adolescents, healthcare providers, educators, influencers, media, and community members to strengthen vaccine confidence, social norms, and support India’s broader cervical cancer prevention goals in alignment with WHO’s 90–70–90 targets by 2030.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This commentary addresses the challenges of HPV vaccine hesitancy and misinformation in India, emphasizing the need for targeted public health communication strategies to improve vaccine coverage and cervical cancer prevention.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary analyzing the nationwide free HPV vaccination drive in India, focusing on the factors influencing vaccine hesitancy among adolescents and the broader public health implications.
analysis_en.methods: The commentary employs an integrated Health Belief Model (HBM) and COM-B theoretical framework to propose a culturally sensitive, evidence-based communication strategy aimed at addressing vaccine hesitancy and misinformation.
analysis_en.main_results: The commentary identifies key challenges such as low awareness, misconceptions, sociocultural beliefs, stigma, safety concerns, weak injunctive norms, parental resistance, urban–rural disparities, and health system barriers affecting HPV vaccine uptake in India.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these challenges as critical barriers to achieving the WHO’s 90–70–90 targets for cervical cancer prevention by 2030, and they propose a multifactorial communication strategy as a novel approach to address these issues.

papers.title_zh: 通过公共卫生传播策略解决印度对 HPV 疫苗 的犹豫和错误信息。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT India witnessed a significant step forward in cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage with the rollout of a nationwide free HPV vaccination drive aimed at vaccinating 14‐y‐old girls. However, the campaign’s success rate can be significantly reduced if timely measures to tackle vaccine hesitancy and related misinformation are not taken into account. This commentary article discusses the effects of HPV vaccine misinformation, identifies global vaccine hesitancy factors, and highlights behavioral determinants affecting HPV vaccine hesitancy and its coverage in India. It identifies low awareness, misconceptions, sociocultural beliefs, stigma, safety concerns, weak injunctive norms, parental resistance, urban–rural disparities, and health system barriers as key challenges associated with vaccine hesitancy and low vaccine uptake among adolescents in India. Using an integrated Health Belief Model (HBM) and COM-B theoretical framework, it proposes a culturally sensitive, evidence-based multifactorial communication strategy focused on raising awareness, building trust, countering misinformation, capacity building of healthcare providers, and enhancing opportunities for the adoption of HPV preventive behavior. The commentary highlights the need to actively engage parents, adolescents, healthcare providers, educators, influencers, media, and community members to strengthen vaccine confidence, social norms, and support India’s broader cervical cancer prevention goals in alignment with WHO’s 90–70–90 targets by 2030.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 印度在 宫颈癌 预防和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 覆盖方面取得了重大进展,在全国范围内推出了旨在为 14 岁女孩接种疫苗的免费 HPV 疫苗接种 活动。然而,如果不及时采取措施解决 疫苗 犹豫不决和相关错误信息的问题,该活动的成功率可能会大大降低。本文讨论了 HPV 疫苗 错误信息的影响,确定了全球 疫苗 犹豫因素,并重点介绍了影响 HPV 疫苗 犹豫及其在印度覆盖范围的行为决定因素。报告指出,印度青少年对 疫苗 犹豫不决和 疫苗 接受率低的关键挑战是认知度低、误解、社会文化信仰、耻辱、安全问题、禁令规范薄弱、父母抵制、城乡差异和卫生系统障碍。它利用综合的健康信念模型 (HBM) 和 COM-B 理论框架,提出了一种文化敏感、基于证据的多因素沟通策略,重点是提高认识、建立信任、反击错误信息、医疗保健提供者的能力建设以及增加采取 HPV 预防行为的机会。评论强调,需要积极吸引家长、青少年、医疗保健提供者、教育工作者、影响者、媒体和社区成员参与,以增强 疫苗 信心、社会规范,并支持印度更广泛的 疫苗 预防目标,与世界卫生组织到 2030 年实现 90-70-90 的目标保持一致。

papers.title: When protein lactylation meets viral infection: A review.
papers.abstract: Lactate is an important metabolic byproduct that regulates protein function under diverse physiological and pathological conditions. Protein lactylation has emerged as a critical regulatory mechanism in virus-host interactions. Lactylation reshapes the tRNA regulatory system during Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) infection and modulates the mRNA processing machinery to regulate host antiviral immunity during severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) infection. In addition, lactylation also regulates telomere maintenance during human papillomavirus (HPV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections. Although an increasing number of studies has revealed have clarified the involvement of protein lactylation during viral infections, a systematic understanding of the interplay of lactylation between host immunity and viral evasion is currently lacking. Herein, we summarize the most recent advances and emerging discoveries regarding the role of protein lactylation in regulating host immunity and cellular responses to lactate during viral infections. We further discuss the mechanistic crosstalk between lactylation and other signaling networks, aiming to broaden the current perspective of lactylation-mediated regulation in viral pathogenesis, ultimately emphasizing this modification as an emerging target for antiviral interventions.

papers.title_original: When protein lactylation meets viral infection: A review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of protein lactylation in regulating host immunity and cellular responses to lactate during human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, particularly in the context of HPV-associated diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, and HPV-associated anal cancer. The central question is how lactylation influences viral pathogenesis and immune responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in understanding protein lactylation's role in viral infections. It does not report a systematic review or meta-analysis, but rather summarizes findings from various studies on lactylation and its interaction with viral infections, including HPV.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Protein lactylation modulates the tRNA regulatory system and mRNA processing machinery during HPV infection, thereby influencing host antiviral immunity. It also plays a role in telomere maintenance, which is critical for viral persistence and oncogenic transformation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while studies have clarified the involvement of lactylation in viral infections, a systematic understanding of the interplay between lactylation, host immunity, and viral evasion mechanisms remains lacking. This indicates a gap in the current evidence base.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for further research to elucidate the mechanistic crosstalk between lactylation and other signaling networks in the context of HPV infections. This could lead to the development of novel antiviral interventions targeting lactylation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the emerging role of protein lactylation in modulating host immunity and cellular responses during human papillomavirus (HPV) infections. It highlights how lactylation influences the tRNA regulatory system and mRNA processing machinery, thereby affecting antiviral immunity and telomere maintenance. While recent studies have clarified lactylation's involvement in HPV-related processes, a comprehensive understanding of its interplay with host immunity and viral evasion remains lacking. The review suggests that further research into lactylation's mechanistic interactions could provide new insights into HPV pathogenesis and open avenues for antiviral interventions.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述是对理解蛋白质乳酰化在病毒感染中作用的最新进展的叙述性综合。它没有报告系统评价或荟萃分析,而是总结了有关乳酰化及其与病毒感染(包括 HPV)相互作用的各种研究的结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 蛋白质乳酰化在 HPV 感染过程中调节 tRNA 调节系统和 mRNA 加工机制,从而影响 宿主 抗病毒药物 免疫。它还在端粒维持中发挥作用,这对于病毒持久性和致癌转化至关重要。

papers.abstract_zh: 乳酸是一种重要的代谢副产物,在多种生理和病理条件下调节蛋白质功能。蛋白质乳酰化已成为病毒-宿主 相互作用中的关键调节机制。在卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒 (KSHV) 感染期间,乳酰化重塑了 tRNA 调节系统,并在血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 严重发烧期间调节 mRNA 加工机制来调节 宿主 抗病毒药物 免疫。此外,乳酰化还调节 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染期间的端粒维持。尽管越来越多的研究表明,已经阐明了病毒感染过程中蛋白质乳酰化的参与,但目前缺乏对 宿主 免疫和病毒逃避之间乳酰化相互作用的系统了解。在此,我们总结了有关蛋白质乳酰化在病毒感染期间调节 宿主 免疫和细胞对乳酸的反应中的作用的最新进展和新发现。我们进一步讨论了乳酰化与其他信号网络之间的机制串扰,旨在拓宽病毒 发病机制 中乳酰化介导的调节的当前视角,最终强调这种修饰作为 抗病毒药物 干预的新兴目标。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述是对理解蛋白质乳酰化在病毒感染中作用的最新进展的叙述性综合。它没有报告系统评价或荟萃分析,而是总结了有关乳酰化及其与病毒感染(包括 HPV)相互作用的各种研究的结果。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 蛋白质乳酰化在 HPV 感染过程中调节 tRNA 调节系统和 mRNA 加工机制,从而影响 宿主 抗病毒药物 免疫。它还在端粒维持中发挥作用,这对于病毒持久性和致癌转化至关重要。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然研究已经阐明了乳酰化在病毒感染中的参与,但仍然缺乏对乳酰化、宿主 免疫和病毒逃避机制之间相互作用的系统理解。这表明当前证据基础存在差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步研究来阐明 HPV 感染背景下乳酰化和其他信号网络之间的机制串扰。这可能导致针对乳酰化的新型 抗病毒药物 干预措施的开发。

papers.title: Maximizing Cytologic Specimen Supernatants: a New Player in the Molecular Toolbox.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple cytologic preparations are available to cytopathologists to use for molecular testing (MT). Proper use of each is necessary to improve patient outcomes. Residual cytology specimens and cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) are novel sources from which nucleic acid may be extracted for MT. CSS may be of particular interest to the cytology community, as it is routinely discarded. If repurposed for MT instead, it may allow pathologists to preserve cellular material from traditional preparations for other ancillary studies. SUMMARY: To evaluate the utility of CSS, it is first necessary to understand the metrics by which MT is evaluated. These include nucleic acid quantity and tumor percentage, the latter of which may be difficult to precisely quantify in CSS. Metrics of nucleic acid quantity include direct measures, such as degradation value (measure of nucleic acid fragmentation), and indirect measures, including many sequencing-derived metrics and concordance with formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue or cell blocks. Specimen contamination and turnaround time are also critical for patient care. Human papillomavirus testing on residual cytology specimens serves as a model of the clinical utility of MT. More recently, studies have examined both the analytic and clinical value of a broad range of MTs performed on CSS derived from both exfoliative and fine needle aspiration cytology specimens and from specimens collected with and without fixative. These studies have demonstrated that CSS contains both cellular (genomic) and cell-free nucleic acid, and that their great advantages lie in reductions in specimen contamination and improvements in turnaround time. Variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality among studies suggest that further specimen optimization is desirable as CSS becomes more widely adopted as a source of nucleic acid.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their associated diseases, specifically examining the utility of cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) as a source for molecular testing (MT). The central question is whether CSS can be effectively used for MT, considering factors like nucleic acid quantity, tumor percentage, and clinical relevance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a broad range of studies that have analyzed the analytic and clinical value of molecular testing performed on CSS derived from various cytology specimens. The methods include evaluating nucleic acid quantity through direct and indirect measures, such as degradation value and sequencing-derived metrics, as well as comparing CSS results with formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue or cell blocks.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The studies demonstrate that CSS contains both cellular and cell-free nucleic acid, and that its use in molecular testing offers significant advantages, including reduced specimen contamination and improved turnaround time. These findings suggest that CSS could be a valuable resource for molecular testing in the context of HPV-related diseases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality among studies indicate that further optimization of CSS as a source for molecular testing is needed. Additionally, the review notes that tumor percentage in CSS may be difficult to precisely quantify, which could affect the reliability of certain diagnostic outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a clear need for research to optimize CSS for molecular testing, particularly in terms of standardizing nucleic acid extraction and quantification methods. Furthermore, the clinical utility of CSS in HPV-related diagnostics should be explored further to determine its potential impact on patient care.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the potential of cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) as a novel source for molecular testing (MT) in the context of human papillomaviruses (HPV). It highlights the advantages of CSS, including reduced contamination and faster turnaround times, while noting variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality across studies. The review suggests that further research is needed to optimize CSS for MT and to assess its clinical utility in HPV-related diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cancers.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 及其相关疾病,特别检查细胞学标本上清液 (CSS) 作为分子检测 (MT) 来源的效用。核心问题是考虑到核酸数量、肿瘤百分比和临床相关性等因素,CSS是否可以有效地用于MT。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述基于广泛的研究,这些研究分析了对来自各种细胞学标本的 CSS 进行分子测试的分析和临床价值。这些方法包括通过直接和间接测量(例如降解值和测序衍生指标)评估核酸数量,以及将 CSS 结果与福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋的组织或细胞块进行比较。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究表明,CSS 含有细胞和无细胞核酸,其在分子检测中的使用具有显着的优势,包括减少样本污染和缩短周转时间。这些发现表明 CSS 可能成为 HPV 相关疾病分子检测的宝贵资源。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究之间核酸数量和质量的差异表明,需要进一步优化 CSS 作为分子检测的来源。此外,该评论指出,CSS 中的肿瘤百分比可能难以精确量化,这可能会影响某些诊断结果的可靠性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 显然需要进行研究来优化 CSS 以进行分子检测,特别是在标准化核酸提取和定量方法方面。此外,应进一步探索 CSS 在 HPV 相关诊断中的临床效用,以确定其对患者护理的潜在影响。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:细胞病理学家可以使用多种细胞学制剂进行分子检测(MT)。正确使用每种药物对于改善患者的治疗效果是必要的。残留细胞学标本和细胞学标本上清液 (CSS) 是可提取核酸用于 MT 的新来源。CSS 可能对细胞学界特别感兴趣,因为它经常被丢弃。如果重新用于 MT,它可能允许病理学家保留传统制剂中的细胞材料,用于其他辅助研究。摘要:要评估 CSS 的实用性,首先需要了解评估 MT 的指标。其中包括核酸数量和肿瘤百分比,后者可能很难在 CSS 中精确量化。核酸数量的度量包括直接测量,例如降解值(核酸片段化的测量)和间接测量,包括许多测序衍生的度量以及与福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋的组织或细胞块的一致性。样本污染和周转时间对于患者护理也至关重要。人乳头瘤病毒 对残留细胞学标本的检测可作为 MT 临床应用的模型。最近,研究检验了对来自剥脱性和细针抽吸细胞学标本以及使用和不使用固定剂收集的标本的 CSS 进行的广泛 MT 的分析和临床价值。这些研究表明,CSS 含有细胞(基因组)和无细胞核酸,其巨大优势在于减少样本污染和缩短周转时间。研究中核酸数量和质量的差异表明,随着 CSS 被更广泛地用作核酸来源,需要进一步优化样本。

papers.title: Modelling the impact of awareness campaigns on HPV transmission dynamics: a neural network-enhanced mathematical model.
papers.abstract: HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection; most sexually active individuals are exposed to HPV at some point in their lives, and the majority of these infections resolve naturally through the immune system. However, persistent infection with high-risk HPV types is the leading cause of cervical cancer worldwide, underscoring the importance of vaccination and early detection in reducing disease burden. In this study, the effect of an awareness campaign on the dynamics of human papillomavirus infection has been investigated through a mathematical model using neural networks. The basic characteristic, boundedness, the endemic and disease-free equilibrium point, and the reproduction number of the model have been investigated. Using the reproduction number, the stability of the model is also investigated. Moreover, a sensitivity analysis is performed to identify the most sensitive parameter affecting the spread and control of HPV. The deterministic numerical solution of the HPV transmission model was first obtained using the ode45 solver based on the Runge-Kutta method; the resulting solution trajectories were then used as training data for a feedforward neural network, which serves as a surrogate approximation model to validate and reproduce the system dynamics. The numerical simulation examines mean square error, validation performance, gradient, and mu across varying levels of vaccination coverage, public awareness, and cervical infection rates. Numerical simulation suggests that vaccination and awareness about the risk of human papillomavirus infection play a crucial role in controlling the spread of the virus in the population.

papers.title: Application of an extended information-motivation-behavioral skills model to predict HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men.
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes substantial disease burden among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM), yet HPV vaccination pathways for men remain evolving in mainland China. Purpose: To apply a culturally adapted, extended Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model to identify psychosocial pathways associated with HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese GBMSM. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2024 and January 2025 among 1,045 GBMSM living in mainland China. Measures included HPV-related information, health beliefs, anticipated regret, subjective norms, self-efficacy, and HPV vaccine acceptability. Measurement and structural equation models estimated direct and indirect pathways. Results: HPV vaccine acceptability was moderate (mean 3.40, SD 1.14). Subjective norms were the strongest predictor of acceptability (β = 0.68, p < .001), with additional positive effects from health beliefs (β = 0.17, p < .01), information (β = 0.14, p < .001), and self-efficacy (β = 0.13, p = .02). Anticipated regret showed a positive indirect effect through self-efficacy (unstandardized B = 0.056, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.12) but a negative direct association with acceptability (β = -0.11, p = .03). Conclusions: HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese GBMSM was shaped predominantly by social norms, with self-efficacy acting as a key pathway through which psychosocial factors were associated with acceptability.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers HPV-driven immune evasion and establishes a TAB2-based prognostic signature in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a key driver in cervical cancer, yet the molecular mechanisms linking HPV to immune escape remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, and clinical data to analyze cervical cancer heterogeneity. scRNA-seq, inferCNV, and pseudotime analysis characterized HPV-associated cellular features and malignant transformation. hdWGCNA identified core gene modules. Univariate Cox, Lasso, and multivariate Cox regressions were used to construct a prognostic risk model. In vitro functional validation of TAB2 was also performed. RESULTS: Eleven major cell populations were identified, with epithelial cells as primary HPV targets. HPV-related gene enrichment increased with disease progression. Malignant cells exhibited significantly higher immune escape scores than non-tumor cells, strongly correlating with HPV infection levels (P < 0.001). hdWGCNA identified three modules linked to immunosuppression, stress response, and proliferation. An eight-gene risk model showed stable prognostic performance across TCGA and GEO cohorts, served as an independent prognostic factor (P < 0.05), and correlated with WNT/TGFβ pathway activation and immune checkpoint genes. TAB2 knockdown significantly suppressed cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. CONCLUSION: This multi-omics analysis identifies transcriptional programs associated with HPV infection and immune escape in cervical cancer. The eight-gene risk model shows potential for prognosis prediction and patient stratification, offering a theoretical basis for individualized treatment. The mechanistic hypotheses generated warrant further experimental validation.

Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers HPV-driven immune evasion and establishes a TAB2-based prognostic signature in cervical cancer.
source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a key driver in cervical cancer, yet the molecular mechanisms linking HPV to immune escape remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, and clinical data to analyze cervical cancer heterogeneity. scRNA-seq, inferCNV, and pseudotime analysis characterized HPV-associated cellular features and malignant transformation. hdWGCNA identified core gene modules. Univariate Cox, Lasso, and multivariate Cox regressions were used to construct a prognostic risk model. In vitro functional validation of TAB2 was also performed. RESULTS: Eleven major cell populations were identified, with epithelial cells as primary HPV targets. HPV-related gene enrichment increased with disease progression. Malignant cells exhibited significantly higher immune escape scores than non-tumor cells, strongly correlating with HPV infection levels (P < 0.001). hdWGCNA identified three modules linked to immunosuppression, stress response, and proliferation. An eight-gene risk model showed stable prognostic performance across TCGA and GEO cohorts, served as an independent prognostic factor (P < 0.05), and correlated with WNT/TGFβ pathway activation and immune checkpoint genes. TAB2 knockdown significantly suppressed cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. CONCLUSION: This multi-omics analysis identifies transcriptional programs associated with HPV infection and immune escape in cervical cancer. The eight-gene risk model shows potential for prognosis prediction and patient stratification, offering a theoretical basis for individualized treatment. The mechanistic hypotheses generated warrant further experimental validation.

It identified eleven major cell populations, with epithelial cells as primary HPV targets, and demonstrated that HPV-related gene enrichment increases with disease progression. Malignant cells showed significantly higher immune escape scores than non-tumor cells, strongly linked to HPV infection levels (P < 0.001). papers.title: Global Lip and Oral Cavity Cancer: Analysis of the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: This study aimed to use the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 Study to analyse the trends in the disease burden of lip and oral cavity cancer (LOCC) at the global, regional, and national levels (1990-2021); to quantify the impacts of population growth, aging, and epidemiological changes on incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs); assess health inequalities associated with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across countries; and predict the burden trends up to 2050 based on the Bayesian age-period-cohort model (BAPC) model. METHODS: Data from the GBD 2021 Study were included in the age-period-cohort (APC) model to evaluate the effects of age, period, and cohort. Decomposition analysis was used to determine the influencing factors. RESULTS: The global burden of LOCC showed a 'high north, heavy south' bimodal distribution with significant sex differences. Decomposition analyses indicated aging and population growth drive increased morbidity and prevalence, whereas epidemiological changes reduce mortality and DALYs. Absolute inequalities measured using the slope index of inequality (SII) revealed indicating persistent SDI-related absolute inequalities. Concurrently, the concentration index (CI) showed that prevalence remained concentrated in high-SDI settings (CI: 0.26-0.13), whereas mortality and DALYs became increasingly concentrated in low-SDI settings. Projections to 2050 show upward trends in age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR). CONCLUSION: Global LOCC showed increasing incidence and prevalence alongside declining mortality and DALYs from 1990 to 2021, with higher burden in males. Population aging and prevalence increases, whereas epidemiological changes mitigated mortality. BAPC projections indicate increases across all indicators by 2050. SDI-stratified strategies are required: human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and screening for high-SDI regions; tobacco control for middle-SDI regions; betel quid regulation and primary care investment for low-SDI regions; and ultraviolet (UV) protection for lip cancer hotspots. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.title_zh: 全球唇癌和口腔癌:2021 年全球疾病负担研究分析。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: This study aimed to use the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 Study to analyse the trends in the disease burden of lip and oral cavity cancer (LOCC) at the global, regional, and national levels (1990-2021); to quantify the impacts of population growth, aging, and epidemiological changes on incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs); assess health inequalities associated with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across countries; and predict the burden trends up to 2050 based on the Bayesian age-period-cohort model (BAPC) model. METHODS: Data from the GBD 2021 Study were included in the age-period-cohort (APC) model to evaluate the effects of age, period, and cohort. Decomposition analysis was used to determine the influencing factors. RESULTS: The global burden of LOCC showed a 'high north, heavy south' bimodal distribution with significant sex differences. Decomposition analyses indicated aging and population growth drive increased morbidity and prevalence, whereas epidemiological changes reduce mortality and DALYs. Absolute inequalities measured using the slope index of inequality (SII) revealed indicating persistent SDI-related absolute inequalities. Concurrently, the concentration index (CI) showed that prevalence remained concentrated in high-SDI settings (CI: 0.26-0.13), whereas mortality and DALYs became increasingly concentrated in low-SDI settings. Projections to 2050 show upward trends in age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR). CONCLUSION: Global LOCC showed increasing incidence and prevalence alongside declining mortality and DALYs from 1990 to 2021, with higher burden in males. Population aging and prevalence increases, whereas epidemiological changes mitigated mortality. BAPC projections indicate increases across all indicators by 2050. SDI-stratified strategies are required: human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and screening for high-SDI regions; tobacco control for middle-SDI regions; betel quid regulation and primary care investment for low-SDI regions; and ultraviolet (UV) protection for lip cancer hotspots. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介和目的:本研究旨在利用2021年全球疾病负担(GBD)研究来分析全球、区域和国家层面(1990-2021年)唇癌和口腔癌(LOCC)疾病负担的趋势;量化人口增长、老龄化和流行病学变化对 发病率、患病率、死亡率 和伤残调整生命年 (DALY) 的影响;评估各国与社会人口指数(SDI)相关的健康不平等;并基于贝叶斯年龄周期-队列研究模型(BAPC)模型预测到2050年的负担趋势。方法:GBD 2021 研究的数据纳入年龄-周期-队列研究 (APC) 模型,以评估年龄、周期和 队列研究 的影响。采用分解分析法确定影响因素。结果:全球 LOCC 负担呈现“北高南重”的双峰分布,且性别差异显着。分解分析表明,老龄化和人口增长导致发病率和 患病率 增加,而流行病学变化则降低 死亡率 和 DALY。使用不平等斜率指数 (SII) 测量的绝对不平等表明,与 SDI 相关的绝对不平等持续存在。同时,集中指数 (CI) 显示 患病率 仍然集中在高 SDI 设置中(CI:0.26-0.13),而 死亡率 和 DALY 则越来越集中在低 SDI 设置中。到 2050 年的预测显示,年龄标准化 发病率 率 (ASIR)、年龄标准化 患病率 率 (ASPR)、年龄标准化 死亡率 率 (ASMR) 和年龄标准化 DALY 率 (ASDR) 呈上升趋势。结论:从 1990 年到 2021 年,全球 LOCC 显示 发病率 和 患病率 增加,同时 死亡率 和 DALY 下降,其中男性负担更高。人口老龄化和 患病率 增加,而流行病学变化则减轻 死亡率。BAPC 预测表明,到 2050 年,所有指标都会有所增加。需要 SDI 分层策略:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 和高 SDI 区域的筛查;SDI 中部地区的烟草控制;对低 SDI 地区的槟榔液监管和初级保健投资;以及针对唇癌热点的紫外线 (UV) 防护。临床试验编号:不适用。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, August 7, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer MicroRNAs identified as biomarkers to triage cervical lesions in high-risk HPV-positive women by Bioengineer August 5, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Cervical cancer prevention may be entering a more precise phase as researchers investigate microRNAs—tiny regulatory molecules that can reveal how human cells respond to viral infection and malignant transformation—as potential biomarkers for identifying cervical precancer. A study published in the British Journal of Cancer examines whether microRNA signatures in cervical scrape samples can help triage women who test positive for high-risk human papillomavirus, or HPV, the virus responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancer cases. The research, led by Laura Valentina Mejia Guarnizo, Carlos Eduardo Trujillo Gama and Liliana López Kleine, addresses a central problem in cervical cancer screening. Testing positive for high-risk HPV indicates that a woman carries a viral type associated with an increased risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, the abnormal growth of cells that can precede invasive cancer. Yet most HPV infections are transient and are cleared by the immune system without causing serious disease. A positive HPV result therefore identifies risk, but does not by itself determine whether clinically important precancer is present. Discover more Pharmaceuticals & Biotech Biological Sciences Health infection That distinction has become increasingly important as HPV-based screening expands. Compared with conventional cytology, which examines cervical cells for visible abnormalities, molecular HPV tests are highly sensitive. Their sensitivity, however, can lead to additional examinations for women whose infections may never progress. Current triage approaches aim to separate women who require immediate diagnostic evaluation from those who can safely undergo surveillance. The study investigates whether microRNAs could provide an additional biological layer of information for making that decision. MicroRNAs are short, non-coding RNA molecules, generally around 20 to 24 nucleotides long, that regulate gene activity after transcription. By binding to messenger RNAs, they can prevent the production of particular proteins or promote the degradation of the messages that encode them. A single microRNA can influence multiple cellular pathways, including proliferation, programmed cell death, immune signaling and tissue differentiation. Because these pathways are disrupted during persistent viral infection and cancer development, microRNA patterns may change before structural abnormalities become obvious under microscopic examination. High-risk HPV can alter cervical cell biology through viral proteins that interfere with key tumor-suppressor systems. The viral proteins E6 and E7 are particularly important: E6 promotes the degradation of p53, a protein involved in DNA-damage responses and apoptosis, while E7 disrupts the retinoblastoma pathway that normally restrains cell-cycle progression. These effects can create genomic instability and uncontrolled proliferation when infection persists. MicroRNAs may reflect the combined consequences of these viral activities, the host immune response and the gradual evolution of precancerous lesions. The researchers focused on cervical scrape samples, material already collected during routine screening. This approach is significant because it could allow molecular triage to be incorporated into existing clinical workflows without requiring an entirely new form of specimen collection. Cells and extracellular material recovered from a cervical sample may contain measurable microRNAs, which can be analyzed using molecular techniques designed to quantify their abundance. In principle, a pattern of increased or decreased microRNA expression could distinguish HPV-positive women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia from those without clinically meaningful lesions. The study’s contribution lies in examining microRNAs as biomarkers specifically within the difficult group of women who are already known to carry high-risk HPV. The key clinical question is not simply whether a woman is infected, but whether the infection is associated with cellular changes that warrant colposcopy, biopsy or closer follow-up. A reliable microRNA-based test could make this second decision more biologically informed. It might reduce unnecessary referrals while helping identify lesions that could otherwise be missed by less specific triage methods. Discover more Genetics OBGYN Women's Health Cancer Infectious Diseases Any biomarker intended for screening must meet demanding standards before it can be used routinely. Researchers must establish how consistently the microRNA signals can be measured, whether the results remain stable across laboratories and sampling conditions, and how accurately they classify different grades of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Performance is usually assessed through measures such as sensitivity, specificity and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Clinical usefulness also depends on whether a test improves outcomes in diverse populations, including women of different ages, ethnic backgrounds and screening histories. MicroRNA testing could eventually complement, rather than replace, HPV detection and cytological assessment. HPV testing identifies the presence of a potentially dangerous viral infection, while microRNA profiles may indicate the biological consequences of that infection in cervical tissue. Combining these signals could support a risk-based system in which women receive management according to the probability of significant disease rather than a positive result alone. The approach is particularly relevant in settings where specialist colposcopy services are limited and unnecessary referrals place pressure on already stretched health systems. The findings reported by Mejia Guarnizo and colleagues add to a growing effort to translate molecular knowledge of HPV-driven disease into practical screening tools. Their work positions microRNAs as possible intermediaries between virology and clinical diagnosis: molecules small enough to be measured in routine samples, yet informative about large-scale changes in cellular regulation. Further validation will determine whether the identified biomarkers can deliver dependable triage in real-world screening programmes. If they do, cervical scrape samples could provide not only evidence of viral exposure, but also a molecular snapshot of whether HPV is beginning to reshape the biology of the cervix in a way that demands intervention. news.content_original: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, August 7, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer MicroRNAs identified as biomarkers to triage cervical lesions in high-risk HPV-positive women by Bioengineer August 5, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Cervical cancer prevention may be entering a more precise phase as researchers investigate microRNAs—tiny regulatory molecules that can reveal how human cells respond to viral infection and malignant transformation—as potential biomarkers for identifying cervical precancer. A study published in the British Journal of Cancer examines whether microRNA signatures in cervical scrape samples can help triage women who test positive for high-risk human papillomavirus, or HPV, the virus responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancer cases. The research, led by Laura Valentina Mejia Guarnizo, Carlos Eduardo Trujillo Gama and Liliana López Kleine, addresses a central problem in cervical cancer screening. Testing positive for high-risk HPV indicates that a woman carries a viral type associated with an increased risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, the abnormal growth of cells that can precede invasive cancer. Yet most HPV infections are transient and are cleared by the immune system without causing serious disease. A positive HPV result therefore identifies risk, but does not by itself determine whether clinically important precancer is present. Discover more Pharmaceuticals & Biotech Biological Sciences Health infection That distinction has become increasingly important as HPV-based screening expands. Compared with conventional cytology, which examines cervical cells for visible abnormalities, molecular HPV tests are highly sensitive. Their sensitivity, however, can lead to additional examinations for women whose infections may never progress. Current triage approaches aim to separate women who require immediate diagnostic evaluation from those who can safely undergo surveillance. The study investigates whether microRNAs could provide an additional biological layer of information for making that decision. MicroRNAs are short, non-coding RNA molecules, generally around 20 to 24 nucleotides long, that regulate gene activity after transcription. By binding to messenger RNAs, they can prevent the production of particular proteins or promote the degradation of the messages that encode them. A single microRNA can influence multiple cellular pathways, including proliferation, programmed cell death, immune signaling and tissue differentiation. Because these pathways are disrupted during persistent viral infection and cancer development, microRNA patterns may change before structural abnormalities become obvious under microscopic examination. High-risk HPV can alter cervical cell biology through viral proteins that interfere with key tumor-suppressor systems. The viral proteins E6 and E7 are particularly important: E6 promotes the degradation of p53, a protein involved in DNA-damage responses and apoptosis, while E7 disrupts the retinoblastoma pathway that normally restrains cell-cycle progression. These effects can create genomic instability and uncontrolled proliferation when infection persists. MicroRNAs may reflect the combined consequences of these viral activities, the host immune response and the gradual evolution of precancerous lesions. The researchers focused on cervical scrape samples, material already collected during routine screening. This approach is significant because it could allow molecular triage to be incorporated into existing clinical workflows without requiring an entirely new form of specimen collection. Cells and extracellular material recovered from a cervical sample may contain measurable microRNAs, which can be analyzed using molecular techniques designed to quantify their abundance. In principle, a pattern of increased or decreased microRNA expression could distinguish HPV-positive women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia from those without clinically meaningful lesions. The study’s contribution lies in examining microRNAs as biomarkers specifically within the difficult group of women who are already known to carry high-risk HPV. The key clinical question is not simply whether a woman is infected, but whether the infection is associated with cellular changes that warrant colposcopy, biopsy or closer follow-up. A reliable microRNA-based test could make this second decision more biologically informed. It might reduce unnecessary referrals while helping identify lesions that could otherwise be missed by less specific triage methods. Discover more Genetics OBGYN Women's Health Cancer Infectious Diseases Any biomarker intended for screening must meet demanding standards before it can be used routinely. Researchers must establish how consistently the microRNA signals can be measured, whether the results remain stable across laboratories and sampling conditions, and how accurately they classify different grades of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Performance is usually assessed through measures such as sensitivity, specificity and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Clinical usefulness also depends on whether a test improves outcomes in diverse populations, including women of different ages, ethnic backgrounds and screening histories. MicroRNA testing could eventually complement, rather than replace, HPV detection and cytological assessment. HPV testing identifies the presence of a potentially dangerous viral infection, while microRNA profiles may indicate the biological consequences of that infection in cervical tissue. Combining these signals could support a risk-based system in which women receive management according to the probability of significant disease rather than a positive result alone. The approach is particularly relevant in settings where specialist colposcopy services are limited and unnecessary referrals place pressure on already stretched health systems. The findings reported by Mejia Guarnizo and colleagues add to a growing effort to translate molecular knowledge of HPV-driven disease into practical screening tools. Their work positions microRNAs as possible intermediaries between virology and clinical diagnosis: molecules small enough to be measured in routine samples, yet informative about large-scale changes in cellular regulation. Further validation will determine whether the identified biomarkers can deliver dependable triage in real-world screening programmes. If they do, cervical scrape samples could provide not only evidence of viral exposure, but also a molecular snapshot of whether HPV is beginning to reshape the biology of the cervix in a way that demands intervention. analysis.brief_en: A study published in the British Journal of Cancer explores the use of microRNAs as biomarkers to triage cervical lesions in high-risk HPV-positive women. The research, led by Laura Valentina Mejia Guarnizo, Carlos Eduardo Trujillo Gama, and Liliana López Kleine, investigates whether microRNA patterns can distinguish between HPV-positive women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and those without clinically significant lesions. MicroRNAs, which regulate gene activity, may reflect the biological consequences of persistent HPV infection, including disruptions in cellular pathways linked to cancer development. The study focuses on cervical scrape samples, which are already collected during routine screening, making the approach feasible for integration into existing clinical workflows. While the findings suggest microRNAs could provide a more biologically informed triage system, further validation is required to ensure reliability across diverse populations and laboratory conditions. The research aims to complement, rather than replace, current HPV detection and cytological assessment methods, potentially reducing unnecessary referrals and improving the accuracy of cervical cancer screening.

news.content_zh: 发表在《英国癌症杂志》上的一项研究探讨了使用 microRNA 作为生物标志物来对 高危型HPV 阳性女性的宫颈病变进行分类。这项由 Laura Valentina Mejia Guarnizo、Carlos Eduardo Trujillo Gama 和 Liliana López Kleine 领导的研究调查了 microRNA 模式是否可以区分患有宫颈上皮内瘤变的 HPV 阳性女性和没有临床显着病变的女性。调节基因活性的 MicroRNA 可能反映持续 HPV 感染的生物学后果,包括与癌症发展相关的细胞途径的破坏。该研究的重点是宫颈刮片样本,这些样本是在常规筛查过程中收集的,使得该方法可以整合到现有的临床工作流程中。虽然研究结果表明 microRNA 可以提供更具生物学信息的分类系统,但仍需要进一步验证以确保在不同人群和实验室条件下的可靠性。该研究旨在补充而不是取代当前的 HPV 检测和细胞学评估方法,有可能减少不必要的转诊并提高 宫颈癌 筛查的准确性。

Spotlight On > ASCO: Esophageal Cancer HPV Infection and Esophageal Cancer — Many pieces of circumstantial evidence, but definitive proof remains elusive by Charles Bankhead, Senior Editor, MedPage Today August 4, 2026 • 5 min read Add MedPage Today on Google MedpageToday In 1976, German virologist Harald zur Hausen, MD, DSc, proposedopens in a new tab or window that human papillomavirus (HPV) causes cervical cancer, countering the widely held belief that herpes simplex virus caused the cancer. Seven years later, he proved the theory, showing that HPV genes are incorporated into cervical cancer cells. Subsequently, HPV has been shown to cause anal, penile, vulvar, vaginal, and oropharyngeal cancers, in addition to cervical cancer. Some patients with esophageal cancer test positive for HPV, which has been linked to other gastrointestinal cancers, notably anal cancer, but also gastric and colorectal cancer. The authors of a recent reviewopens in a new tab or window cited estimates of HPV positivity in esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC), the predominant histologic subtype in the U.S., ranging from 13% to 35%. Estimates vary broadly by geography. For example, a systematic reviewopens in a new tab or window of 15 mostly small studies, published almost a decade ago, showed HPV positivity in up to 93% of EAC specimens. A U.S. study included in the review showed an HPV-positive rate of 16.8%. Much of the contemporary data on HPV and esophageal cancer come from Asia, which has a much higher incidence of esophageal cancer as compared with the U.S. The American Cancer Society estimates that 22,530 esophageal cancersopens in a new tab or window will be diagnosed in the U.S. in 2026, whereas the global incidenceopens in a new tab or window exceeds 500,000 cases annually. In all likelihood, the incidence of HPV-positive esophageal cancer in the U.S. is proportionally smaller. Precise current estimates are hard to come by, but the incidence is "much smaller than what we see in Asia," said Allan Lima Pereira, MD, PhD, of Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida. "If HPV has any relationship in terms of causing esophageal cancers, this would be in the low single digits," he told MedPage Today. "It would be far below the 20% that is often cited from Asian studies." Pieces of a Puzzle As Pereira's comments suggest, a causal link between HPV and esophageal cancer remains controversial. Multiple studies have provided pieces of potential evidence. However, even when viewed from a cumulative perspective, the evidence falls short of definitive. One piece of evidence comes from the observation of papillomatous lesionsopens in a new tab or window in the esophagus, raising the possibility that a virus could be involved in the formation of esophageal cancer. In cattle, bovine papillomavirus (BPV) has been linked to papillomas and carcinomas in the upper gastrointestinal tract. Most BPV infections regress spontaneouslyopens in a new tab or window, but when cattle feed on a specific type of fern, papillomatosis persists and cancer eventually emerges. Studies have shown that BPV has transforming activityopens in a new tab or window in bovine cells. Another piece of evidence relates to the relationship between HPV and cancers that arise in transitional or transformational zones. Most cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, both caused primarily by HPV infection, arise in transitional zones, and transforming HPV infections associated with both types of cancer tend to concentrate in transitional zones. EAC also has a propensity to occur in the gastroesophageal junction, also a transition zone. A study published more than a decade agoopens in a new tab or window showed a significant association between high-risk HPV genotypes 16 and 18 and both Barrett's dysplasia (an esophageal cancer precursor) and EAC. In a separate reportopens in a new tab or window, the same researchers showed increasing viral load and integration of HPV 16 and 18 in association with increasing disease severity, from esophageal metaplasia to dysplasia to EAC. The researchers also found that HPV DNA was more likely to be located in the transformation zone. The dichotomous relationshipopens in a new tab or window between EAC and Barrett's esophagus provides yet another piece of indirect evidence. The historical model of esophageal cancer posits that the cancer arises from chronic gastroesophageal reflux and Barrett's esophagus. Since the 1970s, the incidence of EAC in Western nations has increased by 600%. However, that increase has been accompanied by a decline in the association of EAC with Barrett's esophagus. The association of HPV 16 and 18 with Barrett's esophagus and EAC offers one potential explanation for the anomaly. The rise of HPV-associated oropharyngeal canceropens in a new tab or window lends support to that viewpoint. Since the 1980s, HPV prevalence in oropharyngeal cancers has increased four- to fivefold. Evidence continues to accumulate. A recent meta-analysisopens in a new tab or window that included more than 13,000 patients with esophageal cancer showed significant associations for both HPV 16 and 18. The authors concluded that infection with either high-risk HPV strain "may be a strong co-factor along with other confounding risk factors for the etiopathogenesis of [esophageal cancer]." An even larger meta-analysis published earlier this yearopens in a new tab or window showed an overall HPV prevalence of 31% in 18,913 cases of esophageal cancer. The association with ESCC makes sense, said Pereira, noting that other types of HPV-related cancers are also squamous in origin, such as oropharyngeal cancer. "If you go deeper in the literature, you might find some data suggesting that HPV could be associated with some adenocarcinomas, but it would be very difficult to create a causation," he said. "The impression is that HPV would be more often a kind of a bystander than a driver in adenocarcinoma." Clinical Implications: Not There Yet With respect to clinical implications of HPV in esophageal cancer, the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) does not include HPV in recommended biomarker testing. In fact, the NCCN guidelines for esophageal cancer make no mention of HPV. "But I think it cannot be dismissed entirely. I think it's not over." Issues related to geographic variation, different histologies, methods for detecting and quantifying HPV infection, and other factors confound the reproducibility required to draw definitive conclusions, he added. analysis.brief_en: A MedPage Today review published August 4, 2026, examines the debated link between human papillomavirus (HPV) and esophageal cancer, highlighting circumstantial evidence but no definitive proof of causation. While HPV has been established as a cause of several cancers, including cervical and oropharyngeal, its role in esophageal malignancies remains uncertain. Estimates of HPV positivity in esophageal adenocarcinoma in the U.S. range from 13% to 35%, but incidence is far lower than in Asia, where rates up to 93% have been reported in older studies. However, experts caution that current evidence is insufficient to establish HPV as a causal driver, and clinical guidelines do not recommend HPV testing for esophageal cancer. The review underscores the need for further mechanistic research to clarify HPV's potential role.

news.content_zh: MedPage Today 于 2026 年 8 月 4 日发表的一篇评论探讨了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 与食道癌之间有争议的联系,强调了间接证据,但没有明确的因果关系证据。虽然 HPV 已被确定为多种癌症(包括宫颈癌和口咽癌)的病因,但其在食管恶性肿瘤中的作用仍不确定。美国食管腺癌中 HPV 阳性的估计范围为 13% 至 35%,但 发病率 远低于亚洲,亚洲的早期研究报告阳性率高达 93%。最近对 18,000 多个病例进行的荟萃分析发现,HPV 患病率 为 31%,在鳞状细胞癌中的检出率高于在腺癌中的检出率。然而,专家警告说,目前的证据不足以将 HPV 确定为因果驱动因素,并且临床指南不建议对食道癌进行 HPV 检测。该综述强调需要进一步进行机制研究以阐明 HPV 的潜在作用。

news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 多云 / 24° 隐私 昆明造!首款覆盖HPV58型的三价疫苗获批上市 都市时报 8月6日,记者从康乐卫士(昆明)生物技术有限公司获悉,该公司收到国家药品监督管理局核准签发的三价HPV疫苗药品注册证书,标志着“滇中新区产”三价HPV疫苗正式获准上市。 此次获准上市的三价HPV疫苗是首款覆盖HPV58型的低价次疫苗,能够对亚非地区女性高危型别形成精准覆盖,是HPV疫苗研发领域取得的又一突破。 疫苗研发过程中,康乐卫士在覆盖HPV16/18型的基础上,创新性纳入HPV58型,可将女性宫颈癌的保护范围从70%提升至78%,填补了当前低价次HPV疫苗的精准防护空白。 连日来,位于滇中新区临空产业园的康乐卫士昆明生产基地疫苗生产车间里,生产设备运转,工作有序推进。 “三价HPV疫苗的获准上市是康乐卫士商业化征程的起点,实现了从研发驱动型生物科技企业向具备商业化生产与市场运营能力的综合制药企业的关键跨越。”该公司相关负责人表示,目前公司已搭建起国内布局最为丰富的HPV疫苗迭代矩阵,将加快推进后续九价、十五价HPV疫苗产品上市、市场准入与商业化推广工作。 来源:健康昆明 编辑:马东 审核:钟玲 Free web novels for online reading. 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 艾美疫苗(06660.HK):8月7日南向资金减持7600股 证券之星港... 40分钟前 1 康希诺生物(06185.HK):8月7日南向资金减持15.62万股 证券之星港... 40分钟前 1 河北皮肤硬化面具脸风湿诊疗专家选择参考方向 平安医院免... 2小时前 237 Make Your Own Ocean Pavers Cheaply With This MoldTopchicdeals | SponsoredSponsored Shop Now Undo 想打造自然妈生鼻可以参考哪些技术方向 北京隆鼻医... 2小时前 170 8.8日:阿尔瓦雷斯向西蒙尼递交离队申请!马竞5500万转会费恐成筹码 黎夕爱情 2小时前 749 怎么在昆明选到适配需求的旧房全改及二手房翻新服务 壹山间设计 2小时前 18 2026盘点:昆明无缝管生产厂家哪家好?云南龙铁商贸,为工程项目选对供货商 云南龙铁钢... 2小时前 22 两性关系:70岁夫妻悟透“舍”字,不争不改不盼,往后越活越舒心 暧心情感 3小时前 27 晚餐才是胖瘦的分水线!坚持吃对两样东西,醒来体重直降! 心灵书舫 2026.7.16 1.5万 河北难治型再障诊疗可选择的经验丰富从业者有哪些 平安医院血... 3小时前 236 8.8日:面对全球,用中国话骂中国,高市这次,倒是撞到了朝鲜枪口上 堇墨爱情 4小时前 373 谁在穿越7月北京楼市淡季?改善需求撑起“慢修复”行情 新京报 4小时前 3372 八月八日:不准备打俄罗斯了?乌元首转向中国,对我们外交任务下达,中乌局势又变?
